label: Original-phase input from the 3rd token through <DEL> (ramps up toward the delimiter)
explanation: Fires on every original-phase step from t=2 onward and on the <DEL> step: rate is 0.71 at t=2, about 0.91-0.95 at orig_idx 3-7, and 0.94 at <DEL>. It is silent at t=0 and t=1 and almost entirely silent in the copy phase (0.2% rate, 0.1% of mass). It does not depend on token identity: in_tok, prev_tok, first_tok and n_digits all have flat lift. Magnitude grows within a sequence, rising steadily across the original tokens and peaking at <DEL>, which alone holds 33% of the mass. The largest activations are at <DEL>. Repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire less often (8.7% vs 63%), but requiring in_first lowered F1. Most false positives are at t=2 or on low-magnitude steps.

issues: No systematic counterexample found. All claims check out on test: predicate (t>=2)&(phase<=1) gives P 0.890, R 0.998, F1 0.941, mass recall 0.999. Misses are 4520 steps holding 0.1% of mass, scattered copy-phase blips at small activations.

Factual claims verified on dev profile: silent at t=0/1; rate 0.712 at t=2, 0.91-0.95 at orig_idx 3-7, 0.938 at <DEL>; copy phase rate 0.002 with 0.1% of mass; <DEL> holds 33.1% of mass and the top examples peak at <DEL> after monotone ramps. in_tok, prev_tok, first_tok and n_digits all have flat lift.

The in_first confound caveat is right. Restricted to original phase with t>=2, repeated tokens (in_first=0) fire with precision 0.909, versus 0.875 for first occurrences, so repetition does not suppress the feature. The stored record's 8.7% vs 63% figure is a copy-phase artifact. Adding in_first lowers test F1 to 0.890.

False positives look like noise, not a class. Precision at t=2 is about 0.70 no matter whether in_tok or orig(0) is a digit, in_tok is a vowel, or L is 4 vs 8. Subsets where orig(0) repeats or adjacent tokens repeat sit at precision 0.85-0.92. One mild trend: <DEL> precision falls with length (0.98 for L<=4, 0.88 for L>=8). That is too small to change the predicate.
